limitations: This is source-only machine extraction from the four supplied early-prefix texts, not human labels or a complete leadership history. No later sources, outside knowledge, or other annotator output were used.

Source-specific assertions are retained separately before discussing agreement or disagreement. Repeated mentions of the same role within a source are consolidated with their evidence; repeated sources are not treated as independent proof of realized future service.

Observed_on is the supplied reported publication date, used as the observation date, not a generic validity boundary. Operational availability dates are ingestion/cutoff metadata, not appointment dates.
Future CEO appointments and departures remain planned at the supplied cutoffs. A reported incumbent may have an explicitly planned future end; the qualifier distinguishes that prospective boundary.
For planned negative assertions, status is planned and qualifier explicitly marks negative polarity. Their valid_from denotes intended non-occupancy, never the start of a positive CEO tenure.
The source texts do not supply day-level start dates for Ruggeri’s CFO role, Ruggeri’s interim CEO role, Donahoe’s current CEO tenure, or Friend’s CFO tenure. Those starts remain null.

The Starbucks departure and Nike departure boundaries have competing source readings. No CORRECTS operation is justified because no identifiable correction statement and target appear in these inputs.

No external semantic assumption converts a release effective date into the next day. Nike’s October 13 cessation reading remains explicitly ambiguous relative to the filing’s October 14 effective date.
Exclusions identify role/corporation traps relevant to extraction; general compensation terms, all board memberships, and other non-role biographical details are not exhaustively enumerated.
All evidence spans use zero-based Python Unicode character offsets into each original source text and are checked for exact equality.
